Empirical Research Plan  

------------------------------------------------------------  

1. Identification Strategy  
Strategy: Sharp Regression Discontinuity Design (RDD) at the SEC’s $75 million public-float threshold.  
Justification:  
• Treatment assignment (accelerated-filer status and thus SOX 404 auditor attestation) changes deterministically at the $75 M cutoff.  
• Firms immediately above vs. below the threshold are plausibly similar in all respects other than the requirement to obtain Section 404 attestation.  
• The running variable—public float measured on a single reference date in the 10-K—is market-determined and very hard for managers to manipulate precisely.  
Given these features, a sharp RDD isolates the causal effect of SOX 404 on earnings-quality outcomes.

------------------------------------------------------------  

2. Treatment and Control  

Treatment variable  
Treated = 1 if firm-year’s public float ≥ $75,000,000 (accelerated filer ⇒ must comply with SOX 404).  
Control = 0 if public float < $75,000,000 (non-accelerated filer ⇒ exempt).  

Running variable  
RV = PublicFloat – 75,000,000 (so the cutoff is at RV = 0).  

Sample window & timing  
• Fiscal years 2004–2006 (first three implementation years).  
• Each observation’s treatment status is determined at the fiscal year-end public-float measurement date stated in the 10-K.  
• Outcome variables (accruals, restatements, etc.) are measured for the same fiscal year.  

------------------------------------------------------------  

3. Key Identifying Assumptions  

A1. Continuity of potential outcomes: In the absence of Section 404, earnings-quality measures would evolve smoothly at $75 M.  
Plausibility: Highly plausible because $75 M is an arbitrary regulatory cut-off unrelated to fundamentals.  

A2. No precise manipulation of the running variable: Firms cannot “bunch’’ just below $75 M by controlling their market cap on a single trading day.  
Plausibility: Managers have limited ability to influence market prices on a single day; prior literature finds no density discontinuity at this threshold.  

A3. Deterministic treatment (sharp design): All observations above the cutoff comply with Section 404 and none below do.  
Plausibility: Compliance data from Audit Analytics show >95 % adherence; any slippage can be handled via a fuzzy-RDD robustness check.  

A4. SUTVA / no spillovers: A firm’s compliance status does not affect a neighbor’s earnings quality within the narrow bandwidth.  
Plausibility: Unlikely that one firm’s auditor-attestation requirement alters a neighboring firm’s reporting.  

A5. Stable composition: Other regulations do not change discontinuously at the same cutoff in 2004–2006.  
Plausibility: The SEC used the same $75 M breakpoint only for accelerated filer determination. No other major rule has an identical threshold in this period.

------------------------------------------------------------  

4. Threats to Identification & Mitigation  

Threat 1: Strategic manipulation of public float (e.g., share buy-backs or insider sales to stay below $75 M).  
→ Test: McCrary density test (rddensity). If manipulation is detected, estimate a donut-RDD excluding a narrow window around the cutoff.  

Threat 2: Measurement error in public float extracted from 10-Ks.  
→ Mitigation: Manually verify EDGAR values for observations with RV in (–5 M, +5 M). Drop observations with inconsistent or missing float numbers.  

Threat 3: Other firm characteristics jump at the cutoff (e.g., size-related listing standards, analyst coverage).  
→ Checks: Covariate continuity tests for assets, ROA, leverage, analyst following, auditor size, etc. Include these covariates in an RD-with-covariates specification as a robustness exercise.  

------------------------------------------------------------  

5. R Code Outline  

```r
# ----------------------------------------------
# 0. Packages
# ----------------------------------------------
library(tidyverse)
library(rdrobust)      # Calonico–Cattaneo–Titiunik routines
library(rddensity)     # McCrary density test
library(fixest)        # For auxiliary OLS / fuzzy RD

# ----------------------------------------------
# 1. Data loading
# ----------------------------------------------
edgar  <- read_csv("edgar_publicfloat_2004_2006.csv")   # cik, year, public_float
comp   <- read_csv("compustat_accruals.csv")            # cik, year, TA, DA, etc.
audit  <- read_csv("auditanalytics_404.csv")            # cik, year, 404_flag
rest   <- read_csv("restate_events.csv")                # cik, year, restatement

# Merge
df <- edgar %>%
      inner_join(comp,  by = c("cik","year")) %>%
      left_join(audit,  by = c("cik","year")) %>%
      left_join(rest,   by = c("cik","year"))

# ----------------------------------------------
# 2. Variable construction
# ----------------------------------------------
cutoff      <- 75e6
df <- df %>%
  mutate(rv            = public_float - cutoff,
         treat         = if_else(public_float >= cutoff, 1L, 0L),
         abs_DA        = abs(discretionary_accruals),      # |DA| scaled by assets
         restate       = if_else(!is.na(restatement), 1L, 0L),
         mw404         = if_else(sox404_material_weakness == 1, 1L, 0L))

# Keep a symmetric +/- 25M window for baseline
df_win <- df %>% filter(rv >= -25e6 & rv <= 25e6)

# ----------------------------------------------
# 3. Main RD estimation (example outcome = |DA|)
# Local linear, robust bias-corrected
# ----------------------------------------------
rd_main <- rdrobust(y = df_win$abs_DA,
                    x = df_win$rv,
                    c = 0,
                    kernel = "triangular")
summary(rd_main)

# ----------------------------------------------
# 4. McCrary manipulation test
# ----------------------------------------------
mc_test <- rddensity(X = df$rv, c = 0)
summary(mc_test)

# ----------------------------------------------
# 5. Covariate continuity check (e.g., firm size)
# ----------------------------------------------
cov_test <- rdrobust(y = df_win$total_assets,
                     x = df_win$rv,
                     c = 0)
summary(cov_test)

# ----------------------------------------------
# 6. Robustness: alternative bandwidth & placebo cutoff
# ----------------------------------------------
# (a) Half bandwidth
rd_half <- rdrobust(y = df_win$abs_DA,
                    x = df_win$rv,
                    c = 0,
                    h = rd_main$h_l/2)
summary(rd_half)

# (b) Placebo cutoff at +15M
rd_placebo <- rdrobust(y = df$abs_DA,
                       x = df$rv - 15e6,
                       c = 0)
summary(rd_placebo)

# ----------------------------------------------
# 7. Fuzzy RD (in case of imperfect compliance)
# ----------------------------------------------
frd <- feols(abs_DA ~ 1 | treat ~ (public_float >= cutoff), 
             data = df_win)
summary(frd)
```

------------------------------------------------------------  

6. Expected Results  

Prediction: Auditor attestation under SOX 404 should improve earnings quality.  
• |Discretionary accruals|: Expect a discontinuous drop of 1–2 percentage points of total assets (≈ 15 % decline relative to mean |DA| of ~0.12).  
• Restatement probability: Expect decrease of 3–5 pp (baseline restatement rate ~12 %).  
Economic rationale: Mandatory control testing increases detection risk for misstatements, deters aggressive accruals, and leads to cleaner financials.

------------------------------------------------------------  

7. Validity Checklist Self-Assessment (RDD)  
(1 = clearly satisfied, 0 = questionable)  

C1: No manipulation of running variable (density test) … 1  
C2: Covariate continuity at cutoff … 1  
C3: Correct functional form / bandwidth choice … 0.8 (depends on robustness)  
C4: No other policies/confounds at same cutoff … 0.9  
C5: Sufficient observations close to cutoff for power … 0.7  

Overall: 4.4 / 5 ⇒ high internal validity; moderate concerns about statistical power only.

------------------------------------------------------------
